claim: After launch, Roman is on a steady course to the second Sun-Earth Lagrange point (L2), nearly 1.5 million km away from Earth.
label: TRUE
annotatorNote: [AI label: Claude, 2026-10-06 - not yet checked by the human annotator] NASA's launch-day updates: 'Roman will travel about 1 million miles from Earth to orbit around the second Sun-Earth Lagrange point, or L2'; the spacecraft separated from the rocket after launch. 1 million miles is 1.6 million km and L2 is about 1.5 million km away, so 'nearly 1.5 million km' is within rule 2. 'On a steady course' is only as specific as the launch-day reports.
